When a user logs in, we want them to make their queries using a specific PostGraphile role. Using that role we can define rules that restrict what data the user may access. So what roles do we need to define for our forum example? Remember when we were connecting to Postgres and we used a URL like `postgres://localhost:5432/mydb`? Well, when you use a connection string like that, you are logging into Postgres using your computer account’s username and no password. Say your computer account username is `buddy`, then connecting with the URL `postgres://localhost:5432/mydb`, would be the same as connecting with the URL `postgres://buddy@localhost:5432/mydb`. If you wanted to connect to your Postgres database with a password it would look like `post*************************************mydb`. When you run Postgres locally, this account will probably be the superuser. So when you run `postgraphile -c postgres://localhost:5432/mydb`, you are running PostGraphile with superuser privileges. To change that let’s create a role that PostGraphile can use to connect to our database:
